synthesize_silhouette — 3D space_carving op

• Data kinds: points → image2d

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.synthesize_silhouette(points, K, R, t, size: 'Tuple[int, int]', *, fill: 'bool' = True, dilate: 'int' = 1) -> 'np.ndarray' (to call the implementation directly, import visualhull; visualhull.synthesize_silhouette(points, K, R, t, size: 'Tuple[int, int]', *, fill: 'bool' = True, dilate: 'int' = 1) -> 'np.ndarray'; from the registry, ops3d.get("synthesize_silhouette"))

Usage

Project a 3-D point set into a (K,R,t) camera and return the silhouette (H,W bool) that is True where pixels are occupied.

For GT generation. Projects points (N,3) with X_cam = R X + t and sets to True the pixels hit with depth>0 inside the image. Sparse point clouds leave holes in the projected image, so by default the holes are filled (fill, scipy.ndimage.binary_fill_holes) to give a solid foreground mask. It is then dilated by dilate pixels, giving a silhouette with coverage meaning: "a pixel is foreground if it touches the object even slightly" — this is the conservative rounding that guarantees the visual hull's recall (not missing object voxels) even under discretisation error.

Parameters

points : (N, 3) array_like point cloud in world coordinates (samples on the object surface/interior).

K : (3, 3) intrinsic parameters.

R, t : (3, 3), (3,) world->camera rotation and translation.

size : (H, W) output image size.

fill : bool fill holes in the projected image to make it solid (default True).

dilate : int number of pixels to dilate as a coverage margin (default 1, 0 disables).

Returns

(H, W) bool ndarray silhouette with foreground True.
